Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (an OrcaSlicer fork, C++). Read-only research; do not edit anything. Be very thorough.

Background: the fork added `Plater::notify_project_state_changed(ProjectStateChangeReason reasons)` calls to OrcaSlicer code. Reasons are flags: Selection, Objects, History, Transform, Plates, Project, Settings (enum in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp). Known call sites: src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp lines ~5116, 5172 (lambda `on_committed_transform`, bound to EVT_GLCANVAS_INSTANCE_MOVED/ROTATED/SCALED and maybe others near line 5175), 7421 (`Plater::priv::object_list_changed`), 10465 (`on_object_select`), 11716 (`Plater::priv::take_snapshot`, passes None), 11906 (`undo_redo_to`), 14613-14709 (fork-added select/rename/duplicate/delete/reset), 16922 (`Plater::on_config_change`, Settings), 18300 (`duplicate_plate`); src/slic3r/GUI/PartPlate.cpp ~4478 (create_plate), ~4672 (delete_plate), ~4803 (select_plate), ~4947 (move_plate_to_index); src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_ObjectList.cpp ~4329 (delete_from_model_and_list).

A downstream consumer creates a "manufacturing revision" (a saved checkpoint) ONLY when a notification carries Objects, Transform or Plates. I need to know, for each user edit below that changes the manufactured print result, whether it reaches a notify_project_state_changed call carrying Objects, Transform or Plates (directly, or indirectly e.g. via object_list_changed(), via Plater::update()? — check whether update() itself notifies; I believe it does not), or only Settings, or nothing (for example only `take_snapshot`, which passes None).

Edits to check (trace the real code path for each; cite file:line):
1. Mirror (EVT_GLCANVAS_INSTANCE_MIRRORED or similar) and "place on face", "drop to bed", reset rotation/scale.
2. Numeric move/rotate/scale entered in the object manipulation panel (GizmoObjectManipulation / ObjectManipulation).
3. Painting: support/enforcer painting, seam painting, multi-material (color) painting, fuzzy skin painting if present (GLGizmoFdmSupports, GLGizmoSeam, GLGizmoMmuSegmentation, GLGizmoPainterBase). Also brim ears gizmo if present.
4. Cut, simplify, mesh repair/fix, split to objects/parts, boolean ops, text/emboss, SVG.
5. Adding a modifier / negative volume / support blocker/enforcer part (ObjectList::load_generic_subobject / load_modifier etc.).
6. Per-object or per-part setting overrides edited in the object list settings panel (ObjectSettings, config changes on ModelObject::config).
7. Changing an object's or part's filament/extruder assignment.
8. Layer height range modifiers (ObjectLayers) and variable layer height (adaptive / smoothing, layer_height_profile).
9. Per-plate settings (plate settings dialog: bed type, print sequence, first layer sequence, plate name) and plate lock.
10. Arrange and auto-orient (whole plate or all), and moving the wipe tower / prime tower.
11. Custom G-code / color change / pause inserted from the preview layer slider (custom_gcode_per_print_z).
12. Adding an object (import/load files, add primitive/shape), and "fill bed" / increase-decrease instances.
13. Changing the selected print/filament/printer preset via the sidebar combos (does it reach on_config_change / Settings, or something else?) and editing a preset value in the tab.
14. Anything else you notice that changes the print result but reaches no notification.

Also answer: (a) does slicing ("slice plate" and "slice all") call select_plate / anything that notifies with Plates? (Plater.cpp ~10101 and ~10209 call q->select_plate during slice-all.) (b) In Plater::select_plate (~17664) and PartPlateList::select_plate (~4780-4805): is an undo snapshot taken, and does switching the active plate notify with Plates|History?

Report as a table: edit | reaches notification? | flags carried | evidence file:line. Mark clearly anything you inferred rather than traced. Keep the report under 900 words.

Many edits that change the print result never produce Objects, Transform or Plates, so they would not create a manufacturing revision. You were right that `update()` does not notify: neither `Plater::update()` (Plater.cpp:14531) nor `Plater::priv::update()` (Plater.cpp:5486). `Plater::changed_object()`, `changed_objects()` and `schedule_background_process()` don't notify either (Plater.cpp:17326-17381). Only `object_list_changed()` and `changed_mesh()` do, and `changed_mesh()` does it through `object_list_changed()` (Plater.cpp:17322).

The snapshot-only paths use `take_snapshot`, which passes None (Plater.cpp:11716). `notify_project_state_changed` adds History when undo/redo availability flips (PlaterProjectState.cpp:36-39), but never Objects, Transform or Plates. Undo/redo itself does carry Objects, Transform and Plates (Plater.cpp:11906).

**(a) Slicing.** "Slice plate" (Plater.cpp:10173-10186) doesn't call `select_plate`. "Slice all" does, at Plater.cpp:10209 and again at 10101 for each following plate. Each call goes through `Plater::select_plate` → `PartPlateList::select_plate`. That emits Plates|History (PartPlate.cpp:4803), but only when the plate index actually changes and the list is initialized. So slice-all will look like a Plates change to your consumer. Other callers also switch plates this way: project load (Plater.cpp:6963-6979), preview thumbnails through `select_sliced_plate` (Plater.cpp:17827), and plate clicks (Plater.cpp:18185-18252).

**(b) Plate switching.** Snapshots are taken twice:
- `Plater::select_plate` takes `take_snapshot("select partplate!")` every time, even for the same plate (Plater.cpp:17668).
- `PartPlateList::select_plate` takes another only if the index changed and the list is initialized (PartPlate.cpp:4781-4784).

Both run through `take_snapshot`, so they notify with None. Then, only if the plate changed, `PartPlateList::select_plate` notifies with Plates|History inside a transaction (PartPlate.cpp:4773-4775, 4802-4803). As a result, merely switching the active plate counts as a Plates change, even though nothing about the print changed.
